hypothesis: H3: three-stage curriculum for fno_coreg_residual (S1 LF-pretrain basis-frozen, S2 HF-residual LF+basis-frozen, S3 unfreeze-all) improves composite vs single-stage baseline
hypothesis_validated: NO. Composite_nRMSE is identical to baseline at 0.030408 (0.00% delta), and +9.66% worse than the cycle-008-H1 banked best 0.027729. The fno_coreg_residual family itself regressed catastrophically: heat went 0.026277 → 0.509105 (+1837%), poisson 0.074192 → 0.159364 (+115%). Universal heat kill-switch TRIPPED (0.509 vs 0.0194, 26× over). The H3-specific Stage3/Stage2 heat-ratio kill-switch did NOT trip (ratio 1.0) only because Stage 2 already produced 0.509 on heat — i.e. the curriculum collapsed before Stage 3 even ran. Stage 3 did help on poisson (3.46× improvement over Stage 2 end) but the absolute level remains 2.15× the paper-recipe baseline. Composite is flat only because fno_coreg_residual is not best on either dataset, so its catastrophic regression never enters the composite reduction.
recommendation_reason: H3 makes things strictly worse than H1 banked best on the family of interest: heat regressed ~19× (0.026→0.509, tripping the universal kill-switch by a factor of 26), poisson regressed ~2.15× (0.074→0.159). Composite was unchanged purely by leaderboard accident (this family isn't best on either dataset, so it doesn't enter the geomean). The three-stage curriculum is broken for fno_coreg_residual on this branch — the heat path collapses by end of Stage 2 (stage2_final_hf_test_nrmse=0.509, identical to final). best_val_nRMSE on heat was 0.043 and on poisson 0.022, suggesting the model could fit well at some training point but the final-state evaluation is far worse — likely the eval is using the last-state model rather than best-val checkpoint, or there is severe late-stage divergence (especially in Stage 3 unfreeze-all on heat, though heat shows no Stage 3 movement so the damage is in Stage 1/2). REVERT cycle-008 H3 (commit 420a51c) and re-bank cycle-008 H1 at 0.027729 as the current best.
